problem:
$$
{\begin{aligned}x-\frac{2}{5}y=\frac{1}{5} \\ 2x-\frac{1}{2}y=1\end{aligned}
$$

Find the solution to the system of equations given above.

$x=$
{{field-1}}$,\,y=$
{{field-2}}
worked_solution:
To get rid of fractions, we multiply the first equation by $5$ and the second equation by $2,$ as follows:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x-\frac{2}{5}y=\frac{1}{5} & |\,\times 5 \\ 2x-\frac{1}{2}y=1 & |\,\times 2\end{aligned}\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}5x-2y=1 \\ 4x-y=2\end{aligned}
$$

We will use the substitution method to solve the system. Solving for $y$ in the second equation we get:

$$
\begin{aligned}4x-y & =2 \\ -y & =-4x+2 \\ y & =4x-2\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we substitute $y=4x-2$ into the first equation and solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}5x-2y & =1 \\ 5x-2(4x-2) & =1 \\ 5x-8x+4 & =1 \\ -3x+4 & =1 \\ -3x & =-3 \\ x & =1\end{aligned}
$$

 

Finally, we substitute $x=1$ into the equation $y=4x-2:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =4x-2 \\  & =4(1)-2 \\  & =4-2 \\  & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the solution to the system of equations is $x=1,\,y=2.$
